First-best procurement menu fails the low-cost type's incentive constraint

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006403
Type test case
has calculator text t_L = 480; q_L = 120; t_H = 500; q_H = 100; theta_L = 4; theta_H = 5; U_L = 0; U_H = 0; IC_L = -100; IC_H = 120; feasible = 0
has description in the module Illustrative figures. Paying each type exactly its cost for its efficient output, 120 procedures for GBP 480,000 or 100 for GBP 500,000, leaves both types no rent and satisfies both participation constraints. The low-cost type would earn 100 (GBP 100,000) by taking the high-cost contract, which is (5 minus 4) x 100, so IC_L is minus 100 and the menu is not incentive feasible, the failure Laffont and Martimort show for their first-best contracts.

Five simulations at £30,000 per QALY

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7000263
Type test case
has calculator text lambda = 30000; N = 5; Delta_E_i = [0.40,0.25,0.10,0.30,-0.05]; Delta_C_i = [6000,9000,5000,4000,-3000]; CEAC = 0.6
has description in the module Five illustrative simulations give incremental effects of 0.40, 0.25, 0.10, 0.30 and minus 0.05 QALYs and incremental costs of £6,000, £9,000, £5,000, £4,000 and minus £3,000. At £30,000 per QALY the incremental net monetary benefits are £6,000, minus £1,500, minus £2,000, £5,000 and £1,500, so three of the five are positive and the CEAC is 0.6. The fifth draw lies in the south-west quadrant with a ratio of £60,000 per QALY forgone and counts in favour of the intervention, because the saving per QALY forgone exceeds the threshold. A real analysis would use thousands of simulations.

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006483
Type test case
has calculator text u_11 = 2; u_12 = 0; u_21 = 0; u_22 = 1; v_11 = 1; v_12 = 0; v_21 = 0; v_22 = 2; a_1 = 2; a_2 = 1; q_star = 0.3333; b_1 = 1; b_2 = 2; p_star = 0.6667; interior = 1
has description in the module Slantchev's battle of the sexes (Figure 20). The row player is indifferent when 2q equals 1 minus q, so the column player chooses its first strategy with probability one third, and the column player is indifferent when p equals 2(1 minus p), so the row player chooses its first strategy with probability two thirds, Slantchev's equilibrium. Each player puts the higher probability on the strategy it prefers.

Non-inferiority cell agrees with the one-sided test against the margin

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006584
Type test case
has description in the module Compares NonInferiorityShown with the one-sided test route, the difference plus the margin divided by its standard error set against the critical value, which gives the same decision (derived). With the first worked example the statistic is 3.544 and both routes give 1. Expected result TRUE. A non-inferiority cell written without the minus sign on the margin returns 0 and FALSE, and doubling the cell to 2 or halving it to 0.5 also gives FALSE. With the second worked example (margin 0.05) the statistic is 1.329 and both routes give 0, while a cell that reads the point estimate instead of the lower limit returns 1 and FALSE.
has implementation text =NonInferiorityShown=IF((RiskDifference+NonInferiorityMargin)/StandardErrorRiskDifference>CriticalValueZ,1,0)

Optimal coinsurance rate satisfies the Phelps first-order condition

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006304
Type test case
has description in the module At the optimum the marginal risk premium r sigma squared times C equals the marginal induced-demand loss (1 minus C) times eps mu, Phelps's equation (5a) with the elasticity as an absolute value. The test compares the two at OptimalCoinsRate with a tolerance of 0.001 times r sigma squared plus eps mu, which accepts the rate typed as 0.038 (gap 1.2 against 2.6 for the hospital inputs). Expected result TRUE. For the illustrative hospital inputs, doubling the cell to 0.0769 or halving it to 0.0192 leaves a gap of 100 or 50 and gives FALSE (a halved cell is caught whenever C_star exceeds 0.002, derived).
has implementation text =ABS(RiskAversionCoef*SpendSD^2*OptimalCoinsRate-(1-OptimalCoinsRate)*PriceElasticityAbs*MeanSpendFullPrice)<0.001*(RiskAversionCoef*SpendSD^2+PriceElasticityAbs*MeanSpendFullPrice)
has module record identifier HE-VT-MHHI-003
has test kind domain constraint check
has title in the module Optimal coinsurance rate satisfies the Phelps first-order condition
